summary: A quiet tribal village on one of Gujarat's highest plateaus, grass meadows, ridge walks and valley views without Saputara's crowds.
description:
Don is what Saputara was before the hotels: a small Dangi village spread across a high plateau near the Maharashtra border, sitting at an elevation generally cited as a shade above Saputara's. The draw is simple: open grass meadows rolling to ridge edges, long views over the Sahyadri valleys on both sides of the border, and near-total quiet outside the odd weekend group.

There is no 'sight' here in the ticket-booth sense. You walk the meadows, find a rim for sunrise or sunset, watch village life go by, and in monsoon wade through knee-high grass between low cloud. A handful of viewpoints and small water bodies dot the plateau, and local youths will happily point you along the paths. Basic village homestays and food arrangements exist but are informal: day trips from Ahwa or Saputara are the standard plan.

The access road climbs steeply in its final stretch and is narrow throughout; confident driving or a local driver helps. Go for the emptiness; that is the point.
highlights: High plateau meadows above the Sahyadri valleys
Sunrise and sunset rims without crowds
Living Dangi village, not a built-up resort town
history_legend: Local tradition connects Don with hermitage lore of the epics. The name is often linked in the region to sage Drona. Treat it as living local storytelling rather than settled history.

modes.road: From Ahwa via interior roads toward the Maharashtra border; the final climb is steep, narrow and hairpinned. From Saputara ~55 km via the direct road built in 2013
modes.rail: Bilimora Jn (~140 km) via Waghai; no practical rail access

access.last_mile: Village lanes and meadow footpaths; viewpoints are 10–30 min walks from the village
access.road_condition: Tarred but narrow with a steep final ascent; take it slow in rain

visit.notes: Open plateau; arrive by mid-afternoon if day-tripping so the drive back isn't in the dark.

seasonality.notes: Monsoon for grass and cloud drama, October–January for clear long views; hot, brown and hazy by late spring.

experience.photography_notes: Golden-hour ridge shots both directions; monsoon cloud moves fast, burst through the gaps. Night skies are genuinely dark for Gujarat.

amenities.food: Very limited. A village shop or informal home meals; carry your own food and water for a day trip
amenities.guides: Village youths informally guide to the viewpoints for a small tip

warnings: Ridge edges are unfenced: keep well back in wind or wet grass
The final road climb is unlit and narrow; avoid driving it after dark
Carry all water and food; nothing is guaranteed available

tips: Combine with Girmal Falls for the classic interior-Dang full day
The railed 'photography point' deck on the Ahwa approach road gives the classic plateau-in-cloud frame before you climb
Fuel up in Ahwa; there are no pumps on the Don road
Respect village life, ask before photographing people or homes

faqs.a: Different job: Saputara has hotels, gardens and things to do; Don has meadows, views and silence. Most people day-trip to Don and sleep in Saputara or Ahwa.

nearby.note: The village's own monsoon waterfall and pool
The Anjani caves and kund sit on Don's own plateau
Full-day pairing via the interior roads
